title: Hocile's life in California and her children
summary: Hocile lived in California, sang in a cabaret, had many children, and Sippie raised some after her death.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Was she singing in the '30s? Where was she living in the '30s?
Was she singing during that time?

Yeah, she had an old jealous husband, mean husband. He (unintelligible) fight that night and she had a job singing in a cabaret there (unintelligible) introduced me to the man and everything. She was carrying me back the next day (unintelligible) and oh, so ______. I hate to talk about it.

(Unintelligible). He killed her sister (unintelligible). She thought (unintelligible) and then she went and got the (unintelligible) telegram telling me to come on back to California. I didn't even put the bags down. But she told me on her deathbed to take care of the children, said she was going to die.
Did she keep the name Hocile Thomas for singing in the '30s?
Didn't but seven of them live.
Uh-huh. Well, I guess she didn't use those --
And the man wouldn't marry her.
Oh, dear. The man wouldn't marry her.

But she made life, you know. She got a gun to kill him and instead of killing him, he was after her sister (unintelligible) but me, said, "I hate everybody but Sippie." Didn't never me. Of course, he's dead now. He died of a heart attack last year. I was in California when he died, but I didn't (unintelligible). I was there the day before he died. I didn't know he was going to die, but I (unintelligible).
No, she didn't. I wrote the songs.

She played. Me and her both played. My brother George (unintelligible), but like I told you, his wife run off and left him and Mama raised Hocile from three days old and me and Hocile nursed the same breast.
Well, that certainly makes you close, made you close. No wonder you sang the same if you both nursed at the same breast, indeed.
